angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 150,202 km at 14.96 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 66.8287 +/- 0.0479 mas (same row, RUWE 1.53): 14.96 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.2159 +/- 0.003 solar radii from Cadieux et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 1140 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract): 150,202 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.1844 +/- 0.0045 solar masses from Cadieux et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 1140 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3096 +/- 48 K from Cadieux et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1140 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cadieux et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1140 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-1140.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.035, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1140 (pscomppars): spectral type M4.5 V, from Cadieux et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1140 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.15 dex, from Cadieux et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1140 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.42022, from Cadieux et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1140 (pscomppars): age 5 Gyr, from Cadieux et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1140 (pscomppars): rotation period 131 d, from Cadieux et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...960L...3C/abstract)
